transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I’m just losing hours of my day to rechecking things. It's getting pretty exhausting. I keep checking my dressing supplies, the door locks... even work stuff, like file dimensions and my revision notes. I just, I don't feel allowed to move on to the next thing until I’ve gone through the same routine enough times. I basically have to keep doing it until the anxiety finally drops.
When you feel that urge to recheck, what specific thought or fear is running through your mind?

Well, it's usually this fear that I missed something tiny. Like, even after I know I’ve thoroughly cleaned a wound area, or I've already reviewed a CAD file for work... this thought just keeps cutting in. It tells me I overlooked one small detail, and that it’s going to turn into a serious infection, or a design mistake that actually hurts someone. And the frustrating part is, I can't just reason it away, no matter how much I try to tell myself it's fine.
Outside of these worries about making mistakes or overlooking details, do you find yourself constantly worrying about many other everyday areas of your life, such as finances, health, or family?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, like anyone else, but it's not a constant thing. It's really just the checking. If I know my dressing is clean and the door is locked, and my files are right, I feel fine. I don't sit around stressing about my bank account or, you know, my family getting sick or anything like that. It's very specific to those routines.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 (GAD) as excessive worry is not generalized across multiple life domains, and ruled out F60.5 (OCPD) as symptoms are clearly ego-dystonic obsessions with anxiety-reducing compulsive rituals consuming hours per day.
